paperName: The Operation of Markets and Market Failure

questions.questionText: Which one of the following would not be classified by an economist as a factor of production?

options.text: Labour temporarily out of work
Money in a firm’s bank account
Non-agricultural land
Risk-taking entrepreneurs

questions.questionText: The central purpose of economic activity is the production of goods and services to satisfy needs and wants. Which of the following is one of the three key decisions that has to be taken to achieve this?

options.text: How to achieve economies of scale
What goods and services to produce
Where to locate businesses
Whether to maximise profit or sales

questions.questionText: Figure 1 shows the market demand for electric cars. The shift of the market demand curve from D1 to D2 would most likely be caused by

options.text: a fall in the price of electric cars.
a government subsidy to producers of electric cars.
a marketing campaign promoting electric cars.
a reduction in the price of petrol and diesel fuels.

questions.questionText: A firm hopes to increase its market share by setting its prices lower than most of its competitors. What is the most likely reason for this strategy?

options.text: The firm has a licence that gives it a temporary monopoly
The firm is a price taker in a very competitive market
The firm is aiming to differentiate its products from its competitors
The firm is aiming to increase its long-run profits

questions.questionText: A firm allows customers to personalise a mug with a name of their choice, which it sells for £15. The firm pays £3 for each mug. The paint and labour cost an extra £7. The firm has fixed costs of £150 per month and in a typical month, it produces and sells 60 mugs. What is the average cost of producing one personalised mug?
One reason why merit goods, such as education and health care, can lead to market failure is that

options.text: individuals are unwilling to pay for merit goods.
individuals have incomplete information about merit goods.
merit goods are generally provided free by the government.
merit goods are subject to the free-rider problem.

questions.questionText: Figure 2 shows the market for a good. S1 shows the supply if only private costs are considered and S2 shows the supply if social costs are taken into account. At the free market output, there is

options.text: a negative externality and overproduction of the good.
a negative externality and underproduction of the good.
a positive externality and overproduction of the good.
a positive externality and underproduction of the good.

questions.questionText: Microchips are used in a wide range of products, including mobile phones and traffic lights. If demand increases for one of these products, this affects the price of other products that need microchips. This is an example of

options.text: complementary goods.
composite demand.
joint supply.
substitute goods.

questions.questionText: A firm uses a variety of strategies to improve its market position. Which one of the following strategies is most likely to benefit consumers in the long run?

options.text: An advertising campaign that promotes the product’s image
Charging low prices to drive rival firms out of the market
Investing in research and development to improve product quality
Merging with a rival to reduce competition in the market

questions.questionText: Table 1 shows the percentage market share of firms in a particular industry in 2020 and 2023. What was the change in the three-firm concentration ratio over the period 2020 to 2023?

options.text: A fall of 6 percentage points
A fall of 7 percentage points
A rise of 4 percentage points
A rise of 5 percentage points

questions.questionText: All other things being equal, which one of the following is most likely to result in a fall in the market price of rice?

options.text: Farmers releasing less rice for sale
Good weather conditions for growing rice
More wheat being planted instead of rice
The removal of a subsidy for growing rice

questions.questionText: Which one of the following is most likely to influence the price elasticity of supply of a good or service?

options.text: The availability of spare capacity
The number of substitutes for the product
The percentage of income spent on the good
The price of complementary goods

questions.questionText: Which one of the following is the best example of a situation where there is asymmetric information?

options.text: A firm operating in perfect competition
A seller knowing more than a buyer
Two buyers being equally informed
Two firms working together on a new product

questions.questionText: Table 2 shows the weekly demand for two products, apples and pears, before and after a change in the price of pears. What is the cross elasticity of demand for apples following the change in the price of pears?

questions.questionText: Developed economies, such as the UK, are characterised by high levels of specialisation which involve workers concentrating on a specific task or occupation. This specialisation is possible because in such economies

options.text: an effective medium of exchange exists.
markets tend to have high levels of concentration.
production is concentrated in the service sector.
production tends to involve mainly unskilled labour.

questions.questionText: Figure 4, shows the original demand (D1) and supply (S) in the market for jewellery. D2 shows the demand after an increase in incomes. After the increase in incomes, the market price of jewellery will rise due to

options.text: excess demand at price P1.
excess supply at price P1.
increased average cost of producing jewellery.
increased competition between sellers.

questions.questionText: Following a period of unusually cold weather, growers find that many of their tomato plants have been destroyed, reducing the supply of tomatoes. As a result of this

options.text: the price of tomatoes falls due to the signalling function of prices.
the price of tomatoes rises due to the rationing function of prices.
the quantity of tomatoes demanded rises due to the incentive function of prices.
the supply of tomatoes will fall further due to the signalling function of prices.

questions.questionText: Which one of the following is an example of government failure due to unintended consequences?

options.text: A government target to increase police officers is missed due to a low number of applicants
Government provision of a free flu vaccine for the over 60s has a low take-up
The government cancels a plan for a new railway line after an expensive planning enquiry
The government introduces a charge at a waste disposal site which leads to illegal dumping
